chunks: A man was brought before ʿAlī عليه السلام after he had trampled on a man’s stomach until he relieved himself in his clothes. So he عليه السلام ruled against him that his stomach be trampled until he relieves himself as he had caused the other to do, or else he must pay one-third of the diyyah.

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ فِي ثِيَابِهِ: relieved himself in his clothes as a result of the harm
key_terms.ثُلُثَ الدِّيَةِ: one-third of the blood money due as compensation
key_terms.دَاسَ بَطْنَ رَجُلٍ: trampled a man's abdomen, causing bodily injury
key_terms.فَقَضَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: he عليه السلام issued a legal judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone steps on a man's abdomen until he soils his clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning bodily harm that caused humiliating physical injury. It establishes either equivalent retaliation or financial compensation through one-third of the diyyah, reflecting principles of justice in bodily injury cases.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5326 - In the narration of Al-Sakuni,

it is reported that a man was brought to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) who had trampled on another man's stomach until he defecated in his clothes. Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled:
"His stomach should be trampled until he defecates as the victim did, or he must pay one-third of the blood money (diyyah)."
